Subject: Redwood vs MajorCloud - latency & throughput A/B test follow-up

Hi Tom / Sarah,

Great to demo yesterday — really appreciate the time. As promised, here’s a concise recap and the next steps for the A/B benchmarks comparing Redwood Inference to MajorCloud’s inference API. We want to make sure the tests exercise realistic production parameters so the numbers map back to your traffic profile.

Quick recap of what we discussed:
- Goal: quantify p95/p99 latency and sustained tokens/sec for your 1k–10k TPS slice, and validate tail behavior during bursts.
- Model baseline: open-weights Llama-2-13B (you already run this internally).
- Test vectors: 3 sequence lengths (256, 512, 1024), batch sizes [1, 4, 8], and a short/long prompt mix (60% short, 40% long).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec (sustained), error rates, and token cost per 1M tokens.

Attachments: I attached the benchmark template (globex_benchmarks_v1.csv) and our instructions (redwood-benchmark-instructions.pdf) that include the curl commands and environment variables we used in our lab runs.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) If you can drop your initial run results into the CSV and send back (or upload to the Drive link), we’ll run the same test on our side and line-by-line compare.
2) If possible, include raw p95/p99 percentiles and the token throughput numbers (tokens/sec) rather than only average latency. Tail latency is key for routing decisions.
3) If you want, set up a 30-min sync after you send results — we can walk numbers and propose an optimized configuration (batching, kv-cache settings) that maps to your SLA constraints.

TL;DR — Send the filled CSV + raw logs if possible. We’ll run the mirrored tests, produce a side-by-side p95/p99 and tokens/sec comparison, and propose an A/B routing plan.

Thanks again — looking forward.

Best,

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the templates. We ran an initial pass this morning against our dev sandbox and attached the filled CSV (see attached globex_benchmarks_v1.csv). High-level notes:
- Environment: 8xvCPU + 32GB RAM test runner, GPU-backed endpoints for both vendors (same model config).
- Sequence length 1024, batch=1 (our primary concern):
  - MajorCloud: p95 ~ 162 ms, p99 ~ 412 ms, sustained tokens/sec ~ 5.3k
  - Redwood (your team’s config): p95 ~ 118 ms, p99 ~ 205 ms, sustained tokens/sec ~ 8.1k
- Batch=8, seq=1024:
  - MajorCloud: p95 ~ 210 ms, p99 ~ 520 ms, tokens/sec ~ 27k
  - Redwood: p95 ~ 165 ms, p99 ~ 310 ms, tokens/sec ~ 41k
- Error rates were negligible (~0.1%) for both providers in this initial run.

Questions from our infra team:
1) What exact kernel/quantization settings were you using for the Redwood runs?
2) Any guidance on how to interpret tokens/sec vs latency tradeoffs for bursty traffic? Our prod workload is sensitive to p99 > 300 ms.

We can hop on a quick 30-min call tomorrow afternoon after you’ve had a chance to look.

—Tom

Thanks Tom — this is exactly what we needed. Quick answers and a proposed A/B matrix below.

Kernel / quantization details (short):
- Kernel: fused-attn + custom GEMM path for 1–8 batch sizes; we selected faster FP16 kernels by default.
- Quantization: 4-bit quant (GPTQ) with KV-cache aware dequant path for small-batch inference.
- Commandline snippet (lab): 
  - ./run_benchmark --model llama-2-13b --quant gptq-4bit --batch 1 --seq 1024 --profile p95,p99,tokens_per_sec --out results.json

Interpreting tokens/sec vs latency for bursty traffic:
- tokens/sec (throughput) tells you how many tokens you can push sustainably; latency percentiles tell you the tail users will see. For bursty traffic where p99 matters, prioritize configurations that minimize tail (smaller batch, faster kernels, prefix caching). If you want to route per-request, use p99 as your routing SLO; if you queue/buffer, tokens/sec becomes more relevant for throughput.

Proposed A/B matrix (we’ll ask you to mirror exactly):
- Model: Llama-2-13B (same weights)
- Seq lengths: 256 / 512 / 1024
- Batches: 1 / 4 / 8
- Mix: 60% short (<=256) / 40% long (1024)
- Runs: 3 x 10k requests each (collect p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec)
- Export: raw request logs (timestamps + latency ms) + aggregated CSV

I scheduled Wed 2:00pm PT for a 30-min sync on the Drive link. If that doesn’t work, propose other windows. We’ll run mirrored tests on our infra the minute we have your final CSV and logs.

Best,
Marissa
